newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank cancels liquidity bill auction.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank cancels liquidity bill auction.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Monday said it had cancelled this week's regular liquidity bill auction, the second consecutive week it has done so.
"We did not announce a bill auction again because we consider it unnecessary to intervene with our own instruments given the current market situation," Peter Andresic, NBS chief dealer, told Reuters.
"The NBS has a comparable volume of state T-bills in its portfolio which it can use for sales to maturity date, and not only repurchase its own bills," he added.
Last Wednesday, the NBS took a two billion crown tranche of Finance Ministry eight-day treasury bills into its own portfolio at an extraordinary ministry auction.
Andresic noted that while banks were close to fulfilling their minimum reserve requirements halfway through the two-week period, most of the market liquidity was short-term.
He declined to comment on overall market liquidity.
Slovak interbank money market dealers said the market was "dead" recently, with a few banks in short-term surplus. Overall, the market was short in funds from one month and longer, they said.
Andresic confirmed the central bank's concern over increased T-bill yields, though he said he hoped a recent downturn would continue.
"Any dramatic increase in finance ministry's bill yield could push us to another repo rate hike," Andresic warned.
The NBS repurchases its three-month liquidity bills, on a daily basis, currently for 9.0 percent.
